previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for an allogeneic stem cell transplant from her matched sister following complete remission from CML in myeloblastic crisis. She underwent myeloablative conditioning with fludarabine and busulfan, followed by stem cell infusion on day 6. The hospital course was complicated by neutropenic fever, nausea, vomiting, mucositis, headaches, and a presyncopal episode due to dehydration. She required IV hydration and antiemetic adjustments. Multiple central lines were placed and repositioned as needed. No infections were identified on repeated cultures. Engraftment occurred by day +15, with improving counts and resolution of symptoms. Discharge was delayed due to persistent nausea but was achieved on day +23 with plans for home IV support and close outpatient follow-up.

radiology_notes.text:
TWO-VIEW CHEST RADIOGRAPH ___

COMPARISON:  ___

INDICATION:  PICC.

FINDINGS:  Left PICC terminates just below the expected location of the
junction of the superior vena cava and right atrium.  Cardiac silhouette is
upper limits of normal in size but stable from the prior study.  Small
calcified granuloma is present in the right mid lung.  Lungs are otherwise
clear and there are no pleural effusions or acute skeletal findings.

Comparison is also made to CT of the abdomen dated ___, confirming
the tip of the PICC catheter within the right atrium.

IMPRESSION:  PICC terminates below the junction of the superior vena cava and
right atrium, with tip confirmed in the body of the right atrium by review of
abdominal CT ___.

INDICATION:  ___ woman with diarrhea and diffuse abdominal pain, with
bone marrow transplant one month ago and history of prior typhlitis.

COMPARISON:  ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT-acquired axial images were obtained through the abdomen and
pelvis following the administration of intravenous contrast material.
Multiplanar reformatted images were generated.

CT ABDOMEN WITH IV CONTRAST:  Lung bases demonstrate mild dependent
atelectasis, without consolidation or pleural effusion.  The heart is normal
in size without pericardial effusion.  Catheter terminates in the distal SVC.
Calcified left hilar nodes are consistent with prior granulomatous disease.  A
coarse calcification in the right medial breast is unchanged.

In the abdomen, the patient is post-cholecystectomy with clips in the
gallbladder fossa.  The liver, pancreas (demonstrating mild fatty
replacement), spleen (with focal calcification consistent with granulomatous
disease unchanged), adrenal glands, stomach and duodenum are unremarkable. The
kidneys enhance and excrete contrast symmetrically without hydronephrosis or
renal masses.  The abdominal aorta and its major branches are within normal
limits.  There is no mesenteric or retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy by size
criteria.  There is no free air or free fluid in the abdomen.

CT PELVIS WITH IV CONTRAST:  Since the prior study ___, findings
consistent with diffuse colitis have developed, including prominent wall
thickening and edema involving the terminal ileum, cecum, ascending,
transverse and sigmoid colon, and to a lesser degree, the rectum.  There is
mild mesenteric stranding adjacent to the colon.  The appendix is normal.
There is a small amount of free fluid dependently within the pelvis.  There is
no evidence of perforation.  Scattered diverticula are noted of the sigmoid
colon, without focal inflammatory changes to suggest diverticulitis.

The urinary bladder, distal ureters, uterus and adnexa are unremarkable. There
is no pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy by size criteria.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:  There is no worrisome bony lesion.  No fractures are
present.  Soft tissues are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:
Diffuse colitis and terminal ileitis, consistent with infection.  C. diff is a
possible etiologic agent.  Typhlitis not likely due to distribution and
particularly if the patient is not neutropenic, as current lab results
indicate.

TWO-VIEW CHEST, ___

COMPARISON:  ___.

INDICATION:  White blood cell elevation.

FINDINGS:  Cardiac silhouette is mildly enlarged.  Lungs are clear except for
a linear opacity in the right upper lobe and a small calcified granuloma.  No
pleural effusion or acute skeletal abnormality.

PICC terminates in region of junction of superior vena cava and right atrium.

IMPRESSION:  Small linear opacity in right upper lobe suggestive of linear
atelectasis.  No consolidation to suggest infectious pneumonia.  Incidental
calcified granuloma, unchanged.

HISTORY:  ___ woman with pancolitis, status post colonoscopy,
concerning for perforation.

Supine and upright abdominal radiographs were obtained.

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen, ___.

FINDINGS:  There is no free air.  There is a nonspecific non-obstructive bowel
gas pattern.  There are surgical clips distributed in the patient's right
upper quadrant related to prior cholecystectomy.  There are mild degenerative
changes of the lower lumbar spine.  The visualized lung bases appear clear.

IMPRESSION:

No free air.  No bowel obstruction.

CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS WITH INTRAVENOUS CONTRAST

INDICATION:  ___ woman with pancolitis, status post colonoscopy, with
continued abdominal pain, concern for perforation versus worsening colitis.

COMPARISON:  ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT axial images of the abdomen and pelvis were obtained
following administration of intravenous contrast as well as Gastrografin
orally.  Coronal and sagittal reformatted images were obtained.

CT ABDOMEN WITH INTRAVENOUS CONTRAST:  There is a new small left pleural
effusion.  Adjacent trace atelectasis is seen.

The liver enhances heterogeneously.  The main portal vein is patent, as well
as IVC and hepatic veins.

There is significant increase in abdominal ascites.  Spleen, pancreas, adrenal
glands are unremarkable.  The patient is post-cholecystectomy.  The kidneys
enhance equally and excrete contrast normally.  The abdominal aorta is normal
in caliber.

Again noted is wall thickening and edema involving the terminal ileum, cecum,
ascending, transverse and sigmoid colon.  In presence of ascites, mesenteric
stranding adjacent to the colon is difficult to appreciate.  There is no free
intraperitoneal air or extraluminal contrast.  Again noted are scattered
diverticuli of the sigmoid colon.The appearances in the bowel appear to have
improved overall

CT PELVIS WITH INTRAVENOUS CONTRAST:  The uterus, urinary bladder, distal
ureters are unremarkable.  There is a 7-mm focus of high attenuation, appears
to be in the distal anal canal, best seen on series 3A, image 93.This may
represent enhancement or a localized anal process-clinical correlation is
recommended

BONE WINDOWS:  Demonstrate no concerning lytic or sclerotic lesions .

IMPRESSION:
1.  No free intraperitoneal air and no extraluminal contrast; however,
contrast did not progress all the way throughout the large bowel.
2.  Interval significant increase in ascites, new left small pleural effusion.
3.  Abnormal heterogeneous enhancement of the liver, correlate with liver
function tests.
4.  Slight improvement in pancolitis and distal ileitis.

INDICATION:  Patient is a ___ female with ascites, abdominal pain,
status post stem cell transplant.  Please evaluate for possible ___
disease.

EXAMINATION:  Focused abdominal ultrasound of the liver with Doppler
examination.

COMPARISONS:  Comparison to recent CT examination from ___.

FINDINGS:  No focal liver lesions are identified.  There is no intra- or
extra-hepatic biliary dilatation.  No textural abnormalities are detected.

DOPPLER EXAMINATION:  The right, left, and middle hepatic veins are patent
with appropriate waveforms and direction of flow.  The main portal vein is
patent with appropriate hepatopetal flow.  The right anterior portal vein and
the left portal vein are patent with appropriate directions of flow.  The
right posterior portal vein is not well visualized on this current
examination but was noted to be patent on recent CT examination from ___.
There is a stable appearance of probable hepatic enlargement with inferior tip
of the right hepatic lobe adjacent to the lower pole of the right kidney; this
is unchanged when compared to CT examination from ___.  There is a small
amount of ascites.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Unremarkable Doppler ultrasound examination with patent hepatic
vasculature. The right posterior branch of the portal system is not well
visualized due to limitations of the study.

2.  Small amount of ascites is unchanged.  Appearance of probable mild liver
enlargement with inferior tip of right hepatic lobe seen adjacent to lower
pole of the right kidney, is unchanged from recent prior CT.
